relevance_note: Describes one SSADH deficiency patient and two tested relatives with ALDH5A1 variants: "the patient was found to be heterozygous for two missense variants in the ALDH5A1 gene".
method_note: Hand extraction, no table transcription (Tables 1-2 are mutagenesis primers only). In scope: the index patient (label 'patient', rule 5; 'index patient' is a role word), his mother (sequenced; 'healthy carrier') and his younger sister (tested carrier). The father is mentioned only through 'paternal' variant labels and the 'couple'; he is not described as tested or affected, so he gets no row. His180Tyr (c.538T>C, rs2760118) was left out as a common variant the authors call benign / per se not pathogenic (allelic frequency 0.348), although it lies in cis with Asn255Asp in the patient and mother (the paper studies the double variant His180Tyr/Asn255Asp, which it calls pathogenic; that is recorded in the Asn255Asp functional and parental statements). Val90Ala (rs1272389025, called an SNP and a VUS, later benign) was kept because the paper does not call it common. Patient zygosity recorded as 'heterozygous' as worded ('heterozygous for two missense variants'); the Figure 1 legend says all four family variants were 'present in a compound heterozygous form'. Mother's zygosity left not reported. Cys93Phe inheritance 'inherited paternal' rests on the paper calling it 'the paternal variant'; paternal testing is not described explicitly. For the sister, cDNA/protein fields are taken from the paper's own definition of the same named variants (c.278C>T, p.Cys93Phe; c.269T>C, p.Val90Ala). Contradictions: (1) Methods 4.1 prints 'c.278G>T, p.Cys93Phe; c.538T>C (paternal), p.His180Tyr, and c.763A>G, p.Asn255Asp (both maternal)', whereas Results and Figure 1 give c.278C>T as the paternal variant and His180Tyr as maternal; Results/Figure 1 used. (2) Introduction says 'Cys93Phe and Asn255Ala are pathogenic' while everywhere else the variant is Asn255Asp. Functional statements about variants come from overexpression/knock-in assays of each named variant and are variant-level; patient-fibroblast results were given only on the patient's rows. In vitro treatment of fibroblasts with arimoclomol, betaine and celastrol is not a treatment of the patient, so treatment_summary is not reported. Mother described only as a 'healthy carrier', which excludes no specific checklist feature. 'Mild developmental delay' was not taken as intellectual disability or motor deficit. The acknowledgment of 'Nana, who passed away' refers to an author (Tiegel Nana), not the patient; vital status not reported.
